purpose: Smallest executable retrieval/counter-authority benchmark that can falsify the query-map product: does a plain OpenCaseLaw search (baseline, no query-map/counter-authority machinery) retrieve the frozen controlling authorities for the four observed reality-check questions, in FR/DE/IT, and can an explicit counter/limiting pass reach known counter authority?
baseline_definition: one OpenCaseLaw GET /decisions call per (question, language, channel) with sort=relevance, fields=full, offset=0, limit from top_k — i.e. the same OpenCaseLaw result set WITHOUT query-map reranking, lexicon expansion or citation-neighbourhood expansion

latency_budgets.rule: one search call must return in < 30s; the whole live pass (24 searches) must finish in < 240s

gate_semantics: >=1-of-set per authority/counter gate; a partial-set pass is a PASS naming the missing ids in measured.missing (same semantics as the frozen reality benchmark recall gates)
language_rule: the baseline pool of a question is evaluated per query language (fr/de/it) and as the union of the three; cross-language gates fail when one language's own top-k misses every frozen authority
reproducibility_rule: pass A is fetched live and written to the lane cache; pass B replays the same 24 URLs strictly offline and must reproduce identical raw-body sha256 and identical ordered id list per query
pre_freeze_disclosure: two schema probes with a NON-frozen query (Konventionalstrafe Vertragsstrafe, limit 3 and 50; plus one generic probe query=business judgment rule limit=3 whose payload was only read to the first 400 chars) established response shape, field names, size and latency before freeze. No frozen query text was executed and no frozen authority-hit determination was made before the freeze record was written. The product-cache comparison in the run record is labelled EXPLORATORY because its design followed an exploratory scan of the accepted cache.

id_match_rules.method: a frozen authority id matches a retrieved row when the alnum-core of any of (row decision_id, canonical_decision_id, docket_number, citation_string_de/fr/it) equals the alnum-core of the frozen id; alnum-core = lowercase, drop every non-alphanumeric character, then strip repeated leading court tokens (bgestger, bstger, bger, bge, bg)
id_match_rules.rationale: frozen ids are legacy BGE-style (bger_4A_219_2015) while OpenCaseLaw returns ATF-style ids (bge_4A 219/2015) and citation strings (BGE 142 IV 333); the core mapping is recorded per match in the run record so every hit is auditable

source_validity_rule: every retrieved row must carry a non-empty decision_id, a canonical_url on https with host mcp.opencaselaw.ch, and a language in {de, fr, it}
duplicate_rule: within one query response the alnum-core id must be unique
weak_proxy_disclosure: norm_tokens and limitation_tokens are NECESSARY-NOT-SUFFICIENT lexical proxies (the same disclosure class as the frozen reality benchmark's weak truth gates): a hit shows the retrieved text speaks about the norm and about an exception/limitation term, it does not prove the decision is contrary or limiting authority. Nothing in this benchmark assigns a supporting/contrary label to any decision.
marker_rule: counter::limiting_marker_verified::<slug> passes when at least one COUNTER-channel row's text (title + regeste + snippet, HTML marks stripped, NFKD/diacritic-stripped/casefolded) contains at least one norm_token AND at least one limitation_token; the matching row (id, url, tokens, text head) is recorded as evidence
exploratory_comparison_rule: with --accepted-product-root, the runner scans the ACCEPTED product query_cache search envelopes (params.query present, status 200) and reports, per question, how many frozen authority ids appear in ANY accepted search envelope and in the envelope whose query equals the frozen fr baseline query. TIER = EXPLORATORY (design followed an exploratory scan of that cache before this spec was frozen); reported as discrimination between an unreachable authority (retrieval-side) and an uncited-but-retrieved authority (answer-side), never as a claim-bearing gate.
